disclaimer.title: Read this before you tune
disclaimer.lead: Ryzen Pro Optimizer writes to your CPU's SMU registers and runs intense stress tests. These actions can crash your system. By continuing, you accept the following risks:
disclaimer.safety_nets: Your safety nets: the Esc panic-reset key, the always-visible RESET CO button, the Safety Guard (auto-aborts on temp/voltage/WHEA breaches), the panic-revert breadcrumb (survives BSODs so the next boot can roll back), and BIOS — which always wins on next power cycle.
disclaimer.use_at_risk: Use at your own risk. The authors and contributors are not liable for any damage, data loss, or downtime. If you're not comfortable with that, close this tab now.
disclaimer.dont_show: Don't show this again on this browser (you can clear it via Settings)
apply_confirm.title: Apply these Curve Optimizer settings?
apply_confirm.lead: About to write the following offsets to the SMU. Saving them as a profile first lets you roll back to this exact configuration later.
pro.chart.boost_map: Boost map — voltage × clock (per-core scatter, current snapshot)
pro.chart.hint_toggle: click to toggle · shift+click to solo
desc.test_cycles_hint: Default 1 cycle. 3+ cycles recommended for confident stability. Auto-Adjust typically benefits from longer runs (10+) so each core gets multiple chances.
desc.smart_tune_hint: Smart Auto-Adjust uses bisection + telemetry + crash history. See the Tune Theater for live progress and the Tune Results card for the per-core verdict.
desc.live_co_what: What the chip is running with right now — useful while Auto-Adjust or Smart Tune is changing things. Not what's in BIOS; SMU values until next reboot.
desc.safety_intro: Hard limits that abort Auto-Adjust the instant they're exceeded. Combined with the WHEA Bodyguard, these prevent the kind of silent slide into BSOD that a remote session can leave you blind to.
desc.shutdown_intro: Pick what should stop the service. The server's terminal window (Ctrl+C or closing the cmd window) always stops it — that's the master switch.
desc.settings_saved: Settings are saved in your browser (localStorage) — they survive reloads.
desc.whea_abort: When a WHEA hardware-error event fires during Auto-Adjust, immediately stop, step back one increment on the offending core, and re-snapshot. Default on.
desc.audio_alert: Plays a short browser beep when something dangerous happens — useful if you're away from the desk during a long run.
desc.tabclose_warn: Disabled by default. Chrome's memory-saver and RDP disconnects look like a closed tab and would otherwise kill the service mid-test. When enabled, the server reverts CO to launch values and shuts down after a 3-minute heartbeat silence. Recommended only on a dedicated tuning bench where you trust the browser will stay foregrounded.
desc.escshutdown: When enabled, Esc still resets CO to 0 instantly, but also tears down the server. When disabled (default), Esc is just a panic reset and the service stays up.
settings.tabclose_main: Closing the browser tab/window stops the service
settings.escshutdown_main: Esc key stops the service (in addition to resetting CO)
settings.audio_alert_main: Audio alert on WHEA / safety abort
modes.manual_info_html: Manual test — runs your current CO values through the selected stress test. If any core errors, the report tells you which one and suggests how much to dial back. You stay in the driver's seat.
modes.auto_info_html: Auto-Adjust (autotuning) · per-core tuning — CoreCycler runs the stress test and automatically bumps each core's CO offset upward (less negative) whenever that core errors, then re-tests it. Walks each core to its individual stable edge. Set how far it can back off (Max value) and how aggressively it steps (Increment).
